title: In "time-marches-on", consider moving step 6 "queueing time-update event" to step 1.

labels.name: editorial
labels.description: Changes that do not affect how the standard is understood

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

In the [time march on](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#time-marches-on) steps, step 1-5, is about preparing cues for later process, and does not contain any early return condition in the spec, but in implementation, we can skip the steps, if the media element itself does not contain any track list. Step 6,:
> If the time was reached through the usual monotonic increase of the [current playback position](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#current-playback-position) during normal playback, and if the user agent has not fired a [timeupdate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#event-media-timeupdate) event at the element in the past 15 to 250ms and is not still running event handlers for such an event, then the user agent must [queue a media element task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#queue-a-media-element-task) given the [media element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#media-element) to [fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) named [timeupdate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#event-media-timeupdate) at the element. (In the other cases, such as explicit seeks, relevant events get fired as part of the overall process of changing the [current playback position](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#current-playback-position).)

 which is independent of step 1-5, and should always be run regarless of the result of step 1-5. Changing the order would also not affect the outcome. And we can gain performance from more eager return condition check.
